summary: Discovery for PLG quickstart and evaluation of hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer wants fast time-to-first-token, clarity on free credits, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security/compliance details for a potential pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neal (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Bluefin CTO), Elena Morales (Bluefin Lead ML Eng), Samir Khan (Bluefin DevOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Um, quick intro, I'm Maya, account exec at Redwood. Liam is our solutions engineer who will get into the nitty gritty.
[00:12] Liam: Hi all, hey Ravi, Elena, Samir. Quick agenda — understand your goals, current stack, walk through PLG quickstart and hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, and nail down next steps.
[00:25] Ravi: Sounds good. We're evaluating for an internal pilot to power summarization and a few chat features, timeline is Q1. Primary asks: fast time-to-first-token, low integration friction, and clear security posture.
[00:40] Elena: Also want to know cost profile — our infra team is sensitive to per-token cost and we may consider dedicated if throughput is high.
[00:50] Samir: And from ops side, VPC or on-prem may be required if we go into regulated customers later.

[01:05] Liam: Great context. On the quickstart side, Redwood offers a PLG/self-serve API — you sign up, get free credits, and can be making your first call in under 15 minutes. We usually see time-to-first-token ~5-20 minutes depending on SDK familiarity.
[01:25] Elena: 5-20 minutes — is that with a sample curl or via SDK? We mostly script in Python.
[01:32] Maya: Both. We have quickstart snippets for curl, Python, Node. The free credits we typically grant for pilots — we'll include 1,000 credits for you to run a short eval.
[01:45] Ravi: When you say credits, is that equivalent to tokens? How do we map it to cost estimates?
[01:50] Liam: Good Q. Credits map to $ units that we use in the console. We'll send a pricing sheet showing examples: e.g., model X ~ $0.XX per 1k tokens equivalent. The quickstart credit is to lower friction; you'll still get usage breakdowns in the console.

[02:10] Samir: From a security angle — do you support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS for key management on hosted?
[02:16] Maya: Yes. Hosted supports SSO and RBAC; for KMS we integrate with customer KMS for Dedicated/Private, and hosted offers encryption at rest with Redwood-managed keys. We'll share SOC 2 and encryption docs.

[02:35] Elena: If we start on hosted for speed, what's the path to move to Dedicated? Is it a big migration?
[02:41] Liam: We design for portability. You can pin model versions and config. In practice, moving from hosted to Dedicated is a config and routing change — models stay the same; there may be differences in latency characteristics because dedicated is reserved GPU pools. For high throughput or strict isolation you'd pick Dedicated.
[03:00] Ravi: What about private deployments? We have a few regulated customers and might need a VPC or on-prem option.
[03:06] Liam: Redwood Private is VPC or on-prem. It includes a customer-controlled control plane option, and integrates with customer's KMS/HSM. There's more setup time — typically 6-12 weeks depending on environment.

[03:25] Maya: For your pilot timeline Q1, hosted is the fastest to start. Dedicated could be scoped in parallel if you want to reserve capacity, but we often recommend starting hosted to prove value.

[03:40] Elena: On latency — how do hosted numbers compare to Dedicated? We care about 50-100ms for short prompts.
[03:47] Liam: It depends on model and sequence length. For small models on hosted we often see 60-150ms p50 for short sequences. Dedicated with reserved GPUs and optimized kernel selection can shave that down, especially at scale. We'll provide model-specific perf numbers.
[04:05] Ravi: Any auto-scaling on Dedicated? We don't want to overcommit.
[04:09] Liam: Yes, Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with burst capacity. You can set throughput targets and policies.

[04:25] Maya: Quick question for you — what's your expected QPS and typical prompt length for the pilot?
[04:30] Elena: Initially 5-10 qps, average prompt ~80 tokens, max 300. It's basically summarization and an internal chat assistant.
[04:39] Liam: That fits a hosted pilot. Cost estimates look reasonable. If you scale to hundreds qps, we'd probably recommend Dedicated.

[04:55] Samir: For the pilot we'll need some sample prompts and maybe a small benchmark run. How do we submit those?
[05:01] Maya: Send them to me and Liam — we'll run a short internal benchmark and then give you an estimated latency/cost table.

[05:12] Ravi: One more — data retention and logs. For hosted, do you keep conversation logs? Can we disable retention?
[05:18] Liam: Hosted stores minimal logs for billing and debugging; retention policies can be configured. For strict requirements we recommend Dedicated/Private which gives you control over logs and audit trails.

[05:35] Elena: Any rough numbers for per-100k token cost for the model you recommend?
[05:40] Liam: Off the top: Model A (smaller, faster) might be around $X per 100k tokens, Model B (higher quality) higher. We'll put exact numbers in the pricing sheet.

[06:00] Maya: Quick demo idea — we can provision a demo API key and send a curl + Python example. Do you want streaming for chat or simple response?
[06:08] Ravi: Streaming would be ideal for our chat UX.
[06:12] Liam: Streaming is supported in the API, and function/tool calling is supported as well if you need structured responses.

[06:25] Samir: Are there SDKs pinned to specific releases? We use Python 3.10.
[06:29] Liam: SDKs support modern Python versions; examples in the quickstart repo. Sometimes typos in function names in docs, but we'll link the working snippets.

[06:45] Elena: For the sample benchmark, we'd like to compare it to our internal GPU cluster. What artifacts do you need?
[06:51] Liam: If you can share 100-200 sample prompts and target concurrency, we'll run perf tests on hosted and a dededicated-ish config and report back. We may need a small account for access.

[07:05] Maya: I'll attach the quickstart link and grant the 1,000 free credits. Liam will follow up on benchmarks and security docs.

[07:15] Ravi: On contractual things — for Dedicated or Private, are there minimum commitment windows?
[07:20] Maya: Dedicated is usually monthly or annual reserved capacity commitments. Private has enterprise licensing terms. We'll send the standard SOW examples.

[07:30] Samir: If we do the hosted pilot, but later want a private deployment, do we need to re-run compliance scans?
[07:36] Liam: Typically yes — the private deployment has its own audit steps. We'll help with the process.

[07:48] Elena: Any common gotchas customers hit during quickstart?
[07:51] Liam: Mostly around payload sizes and tokenization surprises — e.g., how tokens count can be different for some languages. Also prefix caching and batching behavior can change latency. We document common traps.

[08:10] Maya: Ok let's go over a quick recap and next steps.
[08:13] Liam: Action items: 1) Maya send quickstart link + credits + pricing sheet. 2) Liam to run short benchmarks once Bluefin shares prompts. 3) Maya to send SOC2/kms docs. 4) Schedule SE deep dive for ops to discuss VPC and private later.
[08:30] Ravi: Sounds good. Can you also share example rollout strategies — canary, A/B?
[08:35] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and A/B tests with automatic fallback policies. We'll include a short guide.

[08:48] Elena: For the benchmark — do you have tooling to replay prompts?
[08:52] Liam: We can share a small harness or you can run Locust/hey with our SDK. We'll provide a sample harness for reproducibility.

[09:05] Samir: Any limitations on model sizes for hosting?
[09:09] Liam: Hosted catalog includes curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. Very large models may be better on Dedicated/private if you need custom quantization.

[09:25] Ravi: Ok let's set a tentative technical deep dive for next week. Is Tuesday available?
[09:29] Maya: I have availability Tuesday afternoon PST. Liam?
[09:32] Liam: Works for me.

[09:36] Maya: Great — I'll send calendar invite and include the quickstart link.

[09:40] Ravi: Thanks all, excited to try the quickstart.
[09:42] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[09:45] End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mislabels; some product words transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "KV cache" spelled "KV cash" in some segments. The SE spelled out policies and we corrected a couple acronyms in post.

References shared: https://redwood.example.com/quickstart (link), pricing sheet (drive link placeholder), SOC2 and KMS docs (link to share).

Recap (short): Start on hosted PLG quickstart using provided credits, Bluefin to share sample prompts, Redwood to run benchmarks and deliver pricing/security docs, schedule SE deep dive next week.
